bindings.note: Greenfield: no rows to migrate, no local writer to retire. Chosen to prove the lineage in production.
Providers are reached over the network. That is TRANSPORT: the send decision is local.
A payment provider being remote is transport, not a remote capability binding. ADR-0003: a request-time access check never calls a payment provider.
Genuinely remote: the vendor control plane DECIDES the grant. The local request-time check reads the projected grant and never reaches a network.

decisions.title: Principal mapping: kernel Party vs ERP employee vs Sub subscriber vs CRM person
decisions.remaining: Fix the mapping between the four models. A subscriber is not a Party, it HAS one; an employee is not a Party, it HAS one; a CRM person is an engagement record. Sub already carries the discipline (party.registry is its canonical Person Party owner, party_contact_points binds observed endpoints with evidence) and the extraction must preserve it rather than flatten it. CONCRETE BLOCKER measured 2026-08-12: Sub's `user_credentials` cannot converge with the kernel's. The kernel links a credential to one `party_id`; Sub links to THREE principal kinds under an exactly-one CHECK (subscriber_id, system_user_id, reseller_user_id); radius_server_id sits outside the CHECK and is a provider reference, not a principal. That is an identity-model difference, not extra columns, and it is the table that stalls Sub's 0.1.0a40 lineage adoption — the programme's first proof. ADJUDICATION IN PROGRESS: ADR-0019 (Accepted, fleet-wide, kernel 0.1.0a41) owns the four-way Party / PartyRole / Account / Principal separation and the rule that authentication binds to a Party while authorization binds to a PartyRole. Record its disposition here once the party worktree lands.
decisions.note: FIRST. Blocks Sub's atomic revision 0001 lineage adoption and the Party principal cutover — nothing downstream can be sequenced until principals map.

decisions.title: The invoice / AR / posting contract between accounting and ISP billing
decisions.disposition: High-level disposition SETTLED: accounting (cap.finance.general-ledger) and ISP billing (cap.isp.subscriber-billing) are separate authorities on separate data planes (ADR-0003). Neither reads the other's tables.
decisions.remaining: The precise contract: what subscriber billing posts to the ledger, in what form, at what granularity, and how reconciliation and correction flow back.

decisions.title: Connected accounts: integration module or product-owned configuration
decisions.remaining: Decide the boundary. account_scope has no source without it, so every thread key and dedup key downstream depends on this answer. A kernel home was prototyped and withdrawn.

decisions.title: Is normalized observation a shared ingress module
decisions.remaining: Product-first proof required. ONE implementation (Sub) and ZERO other consumers today, so the capability is characterizable but not yet extractable. Revisit when a second consumer exists.

decisions.title: Who owns the channel vocabulary
decisions.remaining: Known in three kernel places and validated in none. Modules may not import each other, so no module can be the source for consent, channel policy and delivery alike. A kernel registry was prototyped and withdrawn pending this decision.

decisions.title: Where service teams land

decisions.title: Generic acquisition versus ISP qualification
decisions.disposition: RESOLVED: they are DISTINCT capabilities, not one contested claim. cap.engagement.lead-pipeline takes the generic contract (CRM-sourced); cap.isp.service-qualification stays in the ISP vertical (Sub-sourced, wired to conversation lead links and network serviceability). Neither is a claim on the other.

decisions.title: Retiring Sub's notification queue in favour of the kernel outbox
decisions.disposition: Disposition settled by inventory: Sub's Notification queue and the kernel's OutboxEvent are the same engine built twice.
decisions.remaining: Sequence the retirement; Sub's predates the kernel's and could not have used it.

decisions.title: Template Studio cutover ordering across ERP and Sub
Does ERP adopt the kernel before or during its first module extraction
decisions.remaining: ERP has no kernel, no import boundary and no measurable RLS coverage. Extracting a module into a product that cannot compose it is a plan with no adopter.

decisions.title: Which single complete vertical is step 4 of the programme sequence
decisions.remaining: Step 4 requires ONE complete vertical extraction, not a horizontal collection of packages. Candidates: ISP subscriber+catalog+provisioning, or Backoffice inventory+procurement+assets. The whole sequence waits on this.

decisions.title: A module cannot declare background work
decisions.remaining: ModuleManifest declares api_routers, web_routers, nav, permissions, capabilities, feature_flags, setting_domains, audit_actions and seed — but NOT jobs. There is no task seam in the kernel at all (no celery/scheduler/register_job). The kernel runs its OWN outbox relay and worker, so the capability exists but is not composable. Every product wires background work by hand (Sub and CRM each carry celery_app.py + tasks/). Declaring a job is COMPOSITION and is in scope; building a generic scheduling facility is not — that is explicitly deferred until an extraction is blocked by it.
decisions.note: Readiness gap in composition-spine criterion 6 (router, job, permission and UI composition). Will block ticket SLA clocks and conversation reply reminders.

decisions.title: Compatibility CI proves an EMPTY consumer boots, not that real consumers still work
decisions.disposition: Exact-version upgrade discipline is SOLID: protected-main SHA assertion, version/metadata match, wheel build, dist inspection, publish to the Forgejo private index, then install from the registry and verify.
decisions.remaining: consumer_boot_check.sh proves the wheel boots an EMPTY external consumer importing only the public surface. It does not test a kernel candidate against Sub or ERP before release. Decide whether pre-release compatibility runs against real consumer revisions.
